chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who made a bequest to another, and the beneficiary was absent, and the one to whom the bequest was made died before the testator. He said: 'The bequest belongs to the heir of the one to whom the bequest was made.'

He said: 'And whoever bequeathed to someone, whether present or absent, and the beneficiary died before the testator, then the bequest belongs to the heir of the one to whom the bequest was made, unless he revokes his bequest before his death.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a bequest if the beneficiary dies before the testator in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), narrated by Imam al-Baqir, the principle of 'transfer of bequest' (naql al-wasiyya) is established, ensuring that if the designated beneficiary predeceases the testator, the bequest passes to the beneficiary's heirs rather than reverting to the testator's estate. This legal precedent, found in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, clarifies that the bequest remains valid regardless of the beneficiary's presence or absence, provided no revocation occurred, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preserving the testator's intent and the rights of the intended recipient's lineage.
